note: Waterbody types. Each merged waterbody gets the first type whose 'when' is true, in the order listed. Expressions use the type fields (variables.json type_fields): area_ha, wb_type, on_drainage, stream_order, n_mws, has_drainage_fields, catchment_ratio, and the fields in 'derived', evaluated first. inflow and ownership are unknown from data and are set only by community answers (questions.json type_questions), so without answers the types are exactly those from data.

types.label: Cannot be typed (old layer)
types.description: The layer lacks drainage, stream order and type fields (WB-10).

types.label: Reservoir (out of scope)
types.description: Very large waterbodies, or ones spanning three or more MWS: dam reservoirs and similar. Outside the scope of village-level analysis.
types.why: The 50 ha cut-off and the three-MWS rule are expert judgement: such waterbodies are managed by irrigation departments rather than villages.

types.label: Large river (out of scope)
types.description: Long or wide river stretches spanning three or more MWS or 50 ha. Outside the scope of village-level analysis.

types.label: River reach
types.description: A wet stretch of a river. Its water depends on upstream flow rather than local storage.

types.label: Canal-fed waterbody
types.description: A waterbody on or fed by a canal. Its water depends on canal releases.

types.label: On-stream tank
types.description: A tank of 1 ha or more on a stream of order 3 or higher, often part of a cascade. Typically irrigation storage. On-stream means on a mapped drainage line, or, from 0.5 ha, with a catchment 20 or more times the waterbody's area.
types.why: Stream order 3 or more and 1 ha or more separates system tanks fed by a stream from small check-dam ponds; expert judgement checked against the census tank class.

types.label: Small on-stream pond
types.description: A pond under 1 ha on a stream of order 3 or higher. On-stream means on a mapped drainage line, or, from 0.5 ha, with a catchment 20 or more times the waterbody's area.

types.label: Headwater pond / check dam
types.description: On a first- or second-order stream: runoff harvesting and recharge structures. On-stream means on a mapped drainage line, or, from 0.5 ha, with a catchment 20 or more times the waterbody's area.

types.label: Village pond
types.description: Off the drainage network, 0.5 ha or more: community ponds fed by local runoff.
types.why: 0.5 ha separates community ponds from farm ponds, which are mostly smaller than 0.5 ha; expert judgement. A community answer on ownership overrides the size rule.

types.label: Farm pond
types.description: Off the drainage network and under 0.5 ha: individual or small group ponds.
types.why: Small ponds off the drainage network are taken as farm ponds; the census records most such ponds as privately owned.

derived.note: On a mapped drainage line, or, for waterbodies of 0.5 ha or more, a catchment 20 or more times its area, which catches channel-fed tanks off the mapped drainage line (added 22 Nov 2026 after the census comparison).

derived.expr: (on_stream or inflow == 'stream') and inflow != 'runoff' and inflow != 'canal'
derived.note: Fed by a stream or nala: on_stream from the data, unless a community answer says its water comes from field runoff or a canal; or a stream according to the answer.
